title: Bounded input-head rewind
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean input, let $M$ be a machine with $k$ work tapes and state set $S$, and let $s,t \in S$ and $d \in \mathrm{Option}(S)$. Suppose that from state $s$, on every input and work-tape reading, $M$ moves the input head left and enters state $t$ without changing any work tape or output; and from state $t$, it moves left and stays in $t$ whenever it reads a symbol, while on a blank input cell it moves right and enters state $d$. For every configuration $c$ on input $x$ whose state is $s$, there is an $r \le c$'s input-head position plus $2$ such that after $r$ steps the configuration has state $d$ and input-head position $1$, with all other configuration components unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: Machine $M$ with the specified transition rule in state $s$ for every input and work reading
